title: CONTROL Resonant Items & Equipment
description: Understand the Aberrant, Artifacts and cosmetic bonuses—and avoid confusing Jesse's equipment from CONTROL with Dylan's loadout.
heroAlt: Dylan wielding the hammer-shaped Aberrant in promotional gameplay
sectionDescription: Start with the entry you need. Each file separates its role, practical reading advice and the game it belongs to.

items.name: The Aberrant
items.label: Resonant · transforming melee weapon
items.description: This is Dylan's weapon, not a bag of separately looted swords. It changes shape for different attacks, so learning its Form system is more useful than looking for a conventional weapon shop.

background.label: Wiki classification
background.text: Control Wiki identifies the Aberrant as an Object of Power. That lore category is not a rarity tier, equipment slot or confirmed explanation of every upgrade rule.

items.playerNote: We compare reach, recovery and attack flow when trying Forms. A dramatic silhouette alone is not enough for us to call the damage or a best build.

items.name: Untapped Artifacts
items.label: Resonant · crafting input
items.description: An Untapped Artifact is a find you can shape into an equippable Artifact in the Gap. Keep the uncrafted object and its resulting passive effect separate when reading an item guide.
items.playerNote: Before committing to a setup, read the resulting effect and any activation condition. The original object's name is not a reliable description of the finished bonus.

items.name: Pickpocket's Tool
items.label: Resonant · announced preorder Artifact
items.description: A named Artifact included in the advertised preorder offer. The name does not prove a theft mechanic, extra currency, a loot multiplier or any particular combat bonus.

details.label: Effect
details.value: Not documented in the sources used here

items.playerNote: We would check the exact edition and platform listing before buying. Until the effect is verified, we would not plan an economy build around it.

items.name: Wallet
items.label: Resonant · Digital Deluxe Untapped Artifact
items.description: Wallet is listed as an Untapped Artifact in the Digital Deluxe package. It is an item name, not evidence that the game gives you more money or a larger inventory.
items.playerNote: If you are comparing editions, separate this uncrafted item from immediately usable cosmetics and from early-access terms.

items.name: Communications Department Headset
items.label: Resonant · announced newsletter cosmetic
items.description: The announcement-era Wiki records this headset as a newsletter signup item. Treat it as an appearance bonus, not a confirmed Combat Ability or an Artifact with passive stats.
items.playerNote: We keep newsletter rewards separate from store preorder bonuses. Buying an edition does not automatically prove newsletter eligibility.

items.name: Optical Filtering Goggles
items.label: Resonant · announced newsletter cosmetic
items.description: These goggles are the other signup item named in the Wiki overview. There is no basis in that listing for assigning them enhanced vision, hidden-object detection or a damage bonus.

details.label: Offer status
details.value: Announcement-era listing; current terms must be checked

items.playerNote: We would follow the official reward instructions for your platform. This reference cannot promise that an earlier promotion is still redeemable.

items.name: Service Weapon
items.label: CONTROL (2019) · background, not Dylan's loadout
items.description: Jesse's changing firearm is associated with the FBC Director and the Board. It helps explain why the Aberrant is compared with it, but the two weapons should not share a build list.
items.playerNote: If a guide recommends Grip or another Service Weapon Form, check which game it covers. A CONTROL gun configuration is not automatically usable in Resonant.

items.name: Slide Projector
items.label: CONTROL (2019) · story object
items.description: This Object of Power opens doorways through its slides. Its connection to the Ordinary incident makes it important to the Faden siblings' history, not a normal item to add to a Resonant combat build.
items.playerNote: Read this as story context. The Wiki's Research Sector containment information is not a confirmed Resonant pickup location.

facts: Weapons, passive modifiers and cosmetics serve different purposes.
A preorder item name is not a verified stat description.
The two CONTROL (2019) entries are background references, not promised sequel equipment.
note: We label Resonant announcements, preview observations and CONTROL (2019) background separately. We have not completed a retail playthrough.

sectionTitle: Missions & Quest Types at a glance
sectionDescription: Start with the entry you need. Each file separates its role, practical reading advice and the game it belongs to.

items.name: Dylan's Journey
items.label: Resonant · main campaign category
items.description: This is Remedy's name for the main campaign. It is a quest category, not the title of one mission or a published chapter-by-chapter list.

details.label: Complete mission order
details.value: Not established by the sources used here

items.playerNote: We use the main-story route for Dylan's central objective, but we do not turn the early previews into a complete mission order.

items.name: World Quests
items.label: Resonant · self-contained story category
items.description: These are stories outside the main campaign route. Remedy distinguishes them from the broader mix of encounters, environmental challenges and hidden discoveries.

details.label: Quest names and rewards
details.value: Only list individually when supported by evidence

items.playerNote: Choose a story because its situation interests you; a separate map activity is not automatically a World Quest.

items.name: Faults
items.label: Resonant · previewed activity type
items.description: Published coverage uses Fault terminology, with Metro Fault as a named example. One showcased Fault does not establish how every Fault works, its duration, or its reward.
items.playerNote: Check the individual encounter's evidence before assuming all Faults give traversal upgrades.

items.name: Metro Fault
items.label: Resonant · named IGN preview
items.description: IGN's mission preview identifies a warped metro encounter with train hazards, Mold and the Reach traversal reward. The linked guide describes that published preview, not an independently tested launch route.
items.playerNote: For us, the useful takeaway is the traversal unlock. A preview reward is not enough to give a collectible count, difficulty rating or final clear time.

facts: There is no invented mission order here.
Dylan's Journey and World Quests are categories; Metro Fault is a named preview.
The older Wiki mission directory is explicitly for CONTROL and its expansions.
note: We label Resonant announcements, preview observations and CONTROL (2019) background separately. We have not completed a retail playthrough.

title: CONTROL Resonant Lore & Terminology
description: A player's glossary for FBC files: Altered Items, Objects of Power, resonance and more, with original-game lore separated from sequel mechanics.
heroAlt: A ritual-like interior in CONTROL Resonant promotional media
sectionDescription: Start with the entry you need. Each file separates its role, practical reading advice and the game it belongs to.

items.name: Federal Bureau of Control
items.label: Series background · organization
items.description: The FBC is the secret agency that investigates, studies and contains paranatural phenomena. Its headquarters is the Oldest House. Dylan's complicated relationship with the Bureau is easier to follow if you remember that its personnel, research aims and containment decisions are not the same thing.
items.playerNote: We read a Bureau file as an in-world institutional account. Who wrote it, what is redacted and what the characters dispute matter more than treating it as an all-knowing explanation.

items.name: Altered Items
items.label: Series background · object category
items.description: Everyday objects can acquire strange, sometimes dangerous properties after contact with paranatural forces. The important distinction for a player is that an unusual object is not necessarily something you can equip or bind.

details.label: Not equivalent to
details.value: An Artifact slot or ordinary inventory pickup

items.playerNote: We look at the object's behavior and containment instructions before thinking about loot. A story object, passive Artifact and collectible document belong in different categories.

items.name: Objects of Power
items.label: Series background · bindable paranatural objects
items.description: Objects of Power are a special category associated with the Astral Plane. Many can be bound by people with paranatural aptitude, making their abilities usable. The lore is more nuanced than 'every strange object grants a skill'.
items.playerNote: We separate an object's story classification from its gameplay system. Calling the Aberrant an Object of Power does not tell us its damage, rarity or unlock cost.

items.name: Resonance
items.label: Series background · paranatural energy
items.description: The Bureau uses resonance to describe energies and frequencies involved in paranatural effects. Different resonances can affect people and reality differently; the Hiss is not a synonym for every supernatural force.
items.playerNote: When a scene mentions a new resonance, avoid assuming it has the Hiss's exact behavior. The term provides a story framework, not a universal elemental weakness chart.

items.name: Altered World Event
items.label: Series background · incident classification
items.description: An AWE is an intrusion of paranatural forces that changes ordinary reality. Such incidents are central to the Bureau's investigations and can involve altered objects or other phenomena.

details.label: Separate use of the name
details.value: AWE is also the title of CONTROL's second expansion

items.playerNote: Check the context when a guide says AWE: it may mean a type of incident, or the older downloadable expansion. Neither meaning gives you a Resonant quest name by itself.

items.name: Parautilitarian
items.label: Series background · person with paranatural abilities
items.description: A parautilitarian is someone who demonstrates paranatural abilities. Those abilities can have different origins, including personal aptitude or connections with entities and objects. Jesse and Dylan are important examples.

details.label: Describes
details.value: A person and their paranatural capacity

items.playerNote: Treat the word as a Bureau description of a person, not an RPG class selection. Dylan's playable setup is explained through Forms, Combat Abilities, Talents and Artifacts.

facts: This glossary explains the fiction; it does not assign hidden gameplay stats.
A collectible file about an object and the object itself are different entries.
New players can use the definitions without reading complete character biographies.
note: We label Resonant announcements, preview observations and CONTROL (2019) background separately. We have not completed a retail playthrough.

title: CONTROL Resonant Locations
description: Know the difference between Manhattan, the West Incursion Zone, the Gap and the Oldest House before following a location or mission guide.
heroAlt: Dylan overlooking distorted Manhattan in official promotional media
sectionDescription: Start with the entry you need. Each file separates its role, practical reading advice and the game it belongs to.

items.name: Manhattan
items.label: Resonant · main setting
items.description: Dylan's journey takes place in a transformed Manhattan. The city is the broader setting; it should not be treated as one mission area with a single collectible total.

details.label: World structure
details.value: Distinct designed zones, not a conventional open-world checklist

items.playerNote: When we use a location guide, we check the Zone and named activity first. A city-wide screenshot is not enough for a precise pickup location.

items.name: West Incursion Zone
items.label: Resonant · officially named gameplay area
items.description: Remedy identifies this area in the first gameplay presentation. It is a concrete location name to recognize when comparing preview footage and exploration coverage.
items.playerNote: Gravity-altered geometry makes the direction of travel important. Follow the demonstrated surfaces and route context instead of assuming a normal street map explains the space.

items.name: The Gap
items.label: Resonant · build-management space
items.description: The Gap is a dreamlike space tied to Dylan. Its practical role is build management: it is where you think about abilities, Forms and upgrades rather than another neighborhood to clear.
items.playerNote: We use the build guides to change a setup and the map or mission indexes to travel. The Gap and a physical destination solve different problems.

items.name: Oldest House
items.label: Series background · Bureau headquarters
items.description: The changing brutalist building is the FBC headquarters and the main setting of CONTROL (2019). Its familiar sectors explain older guide terminology, but do not establish where Dylan can go in Resonant.
items.playerNote: A Research Sector collectible coordinate from Jesse's game is not a Manhattan collectible coordinate. Check the game title before following any older route.

facts: Locations, quest categories and traversal abilities are indexed separately.
The Oldest House entry supplies background, not a claimed complete Resonant interior map.
No unverified collectible pins or percentage-complete maps are supplied.
note: We label Resonant announcements, preview observations and CONTROL (2019) background separately. We have not completed a retail playthrough.
